review.authorization: Active goal and standing autonomous approval for documented native screening reconstructions.
review.basis: Original heat-CCS useful-heat/90%-capture/8%-penalty model, reconciled to the inspected native allocated stack.
limitations: Reconstruct a 1 MJ useful-heat screening service on complete native German natural-gas CHP heat plus the normal CLIC post-combustion capture, 200 km pipeline and 1000 m storage chain. Native allocation, technology, geography, vintage, capture energy and storage assumptions differ; score effects are unquantified.

Retain the original heat-CCS model’s 8% heat-input penalty and 90% capture of attributable allocated combustion CO2. Native heat draws 0.64 MJ of burned-gas service per MJ; that service reports 0.0561 kg fossil CO2/MJ. Apply 1.08 MJ native heat and 0.034898688 kg captured service and subtract the same CO2 once. This replaces the source 0.021910824 kg capture quantity, which would yield only 56.5057% capture on this native heat basis. Do not infer physical heat efficiency by inverting the allocated fuel input.

Capture-chain energy, transport, storage leakage and infrastructure remain complete. The negative stack correction excludes those upstream burdens; no extra heat/electricity credit or second avoided-emission credit is added. Preserve the shared fuels update’s recorded-total/carbon-origin conventions and explicitly check the combined update before qualifying it.

The complete German CHP heat supplier is held through a fixed-reference bridge so standard regional relinking cannot substitute a different allocated stack while retaining a fixed capture quantity. This is an explicit German technology/geography proxy in all IAM regions. The bridge adds no physical burden, credit or second loss factor.
